key_insight: Graph neural networks predict dissociative water adsorption on nickel from bare-metal geometry, without constructing or relaxing adsorbates during screening.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables efficient screening of OH*+H* binding configurations on nickel nanoparticles containing up to approximately 3,000 atoms.
method: Define candidate O- and H-binding sites using sets of Ni anchor atoms.
Build graphs from anchors and their local Ni environment in MACE-relaxed bare geometries.
Use separate GNNs to predict adsorption energy and binding-site retention after DFT relaxation.
evidence_signal: The energy model achieves 0.031 eV internal-validation MAE; independent tests on unseen Ni55, Ni91, Ni130 clusters and larger surface cells support transferability, especially for relative-energy ranking.
watch_item: Quantitative accuracy varies across systems, so energy predictions and conservative retention filtering require validation for new screening targets.
paper_title: Adsorbate-Free Screening of Dissociative Water Adsorption on Nickel Nanoparticles via Graph Neural Networks
